children: November 18 (Renewables Now) - Siemens Gamesa has been selected as the turbine supplier for the 1-GW first phase of the Zeevonk offshore wind project in the Dutch North Sea, which is being jointly developed by Vattenfall and Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP).

The manufacturer will deliver 69 turbines, each with a nominal capacity of 15 MW, and will also provide long-term service and maintenance for the wind farm under a separate service and warranty agreement. Production of the turbines is planned for 2028, with installation expected in 2029.

With the selection of Siemens Gamesa all key supplier agreements for the construction phase of Zeevonk Phase I are now in place, Vattenfall said today. It follows contracts with TKF, EEW Group, DEME and Boskalis.

“The signing of the turbine supply agreement and the service and warranty agreement represents a major milestone for Zeevonk. With the project’s two largest contracts now in place, we are moving decisively towards a final investment decision and bringing Zeevonk into execution,” said Felix Pahl, partner at CIP.

The SG 15-236 turbines will feature 115-metre-long blades and multiple of them will incorporate Siemens Gamesa's GreenerTower technology, which uses low-emission steel, and its RecyclableBlade technology.

The Zeevonk project will be located 63 to 84 km off the coast. Its first phase will be followed by Phase 2 in 2032, which will add another 1 GW of wind energy and 500 MW of system integration capacity. The latter will include an electrolysis plant at the Port of Rotterdam for the production of green hydrogen.
Siemens Gamesa’s parent, Siemens Energy, recently reported that the wind turbine business achieved break-even for the fiscal year through September.

title: Siemens Gamesa offshore wind turbines picked for 1-GW Zeevonk Phase I
